question: A 58-year-old obese male has noticed the gradual development of a soft bulge on his right groin that has been present over the past year and occasionally becomes very tender. He notices that it comes out when he coughs and strains during bowel movements. He is able to push the bulge back in without issue. After examination, you realize that he has an inguinal hernia and recommend open repair with mesh placement. After surgery, the patient returns to clinic and complains of numbness and tingling in the upper part of the scrotum and base of the penis. What nerve was most likely injured during the procedure?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Inguinal hernia repair" -> "Potential nerve injury during surgery" -> "Numbness and tingling in the upper scrotum" -> "Involvement of the genitofemoral nerve" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Inguinal hernia repair" -> "Surgical manipulation in the groin area" -> "Possible damage to nearby nerves" -> "Symptoms localized to the scrotum and penis" -> "Genitofemoral nerve likely affected" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with numbness and tingling" -> "Symptoms suggest nerve involvement" -> "Location of symptoms indicates possible nerve injury" -> "Genitofemoral nerve supplies sensation to the scrotum" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Surgical procedure in the inguinal region" -> "Risk of nerve injury" -> "Numbness in the upper scrotum and base of the penis" -> "Genitofemoral nerve is responsible for this area" -> 88%
enhanced_information: Inguinal hernia repair is associated with the risk of nerve injury due to the proximity of several nerves in the groin area. The symptoms of numbness and tingling in the upper part of the scrotum and base of the penis suggest involvement of the genitofemoral nerve, which provides sensory innervation to this region. The reasoning chains consistently point to the genitofemoral nerve as the likely affected nerve, supported by the consensus that this nerve is responsible for sensation in the scrotum. Other options, such as the iliohypogastric nerve, ilioinguinal nerve, lateral femoral cutaneous nerve, and obturator nerve, do not correlate with the specific symptoms presented. Therefore, the most likely nerve injured during the procedure is the genitofemoral nerve.
analysis: Inguinal hernia repair can lead to nerve injuries due to the close anatomical relationships of various nerves in the groin area. The symptoms described by the patient—numbness and tingling in the upper part of the scrotum and base of the penis—are indicative of sensory nerve involvement. The genitofemoral nerve is responsible for providing sensory innervation to the skin of the scrotum and the upper thigh, which aligns with the patient's symptoms. The ilioinguinal nerve also provides sensation to the groin and part of the scrotum, but the specific symptoms of tingling and numbness in the upper scrotum and base of the penis more strongly suggest involvement of the genitofemoral nerve. Other nerves listed, such as the iliohypogastric, lateral femoral cutaneous, and obturator nerves, do not correlate with the sensory distribution affected in this case. Therefore, the most likely nerve injured during the procedure is the genitofemoral nerve.
